title: Erasmian Koine Greek alphabet — app clip pack
notes: Each clip is name then sound. Master file inserts 1.60s silence between clips for easy snipping. Cue times are for the master file. Two rows were regenerated later and are not in the master: they carry source, take and a note instead of master offsets. Each row carries a sha1 of its mp3, checked by tools/check_sounds.py, so a clip cannot be replaced without the record of what was spoken moving with it.

clips.cue: /aɪˈjoʊtaː/ … ih, as in pit, or ee, as in machine
clips.note: A SPLICE, chosen by ear: the name from the previous clip (Fraser preferred how it said 'iota'), 0 to 1.06 s, joined to the sounds of take bI1_0_c from 1.30 s, each cut inside a pause with a 30 ms fade, leaving a 0.30 s gap -- the old clip's own. Loudness within about 1 dB. Chosen over the unspliced bI1_0_c and a 0.40 s-gap splice. Iota and upsilon, the two letters lesson 1 gives two sounds, both say the lesson's example words.

clips.note: chosen by ear over the shipping clip and two other renderings — lesson 1's own words carry both sounds. The only letter clip that gives example words, and chosen for it: upsilon's short sound came out as its long one in every other arrangement tried. Lesson 1 gives example words for most letters, so the clip matches the lesson's own way of teaching.
clips.cue: /ˈʊpsɪlɒn/ … /uː/, as in lute, or /ʊ/, as in put

clips.name: Chi
clips.note: Both halves were rejected: the name came out with the soft ch of 'church' instead of /kaI/, and the sound came out as the WORD 'Bach'. Recued 'Kai.  Khh.' in one take, sound half lifted 5 dB. This clip settles what chi is: its sound measures 260 ms of sustained energy at zero-crossing 0.22-0.28, which is frication, not the burst-plus-tail of an aspirated stop. So it is the loch sound lesson 1 teaches, and chi stays a declared departure from Black's 'chemist'. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Psi
clips.note: chosen by ear over the shipping clip and two other renderings — a helper vowel so the p is heard, as psai. A helper vowel before the name, because English cannot open a word with /ps/ and drops the p -- the same cluster as πν in πνευματικός.

notes_2026_09_23: Re-cued 2026-09-23 after a learner reported the letter sounds getting cut off too quickly. The cut-off was the master's splice: every clip had been cut from one file with a fixed pad. 28 of the 32 clips are now generated one at a time in IPA and were chosen by ear over the master clip and two other renderings; each such row records its cue, source and a note, and carries no master_start/master_end. Chi was already a separate take, regenerated 2026-09-09 as the loch sound, and the ear kept it again. The three still cut from the master are the ones the ear preferred as they were: 03_gamma, 04_delta, 05_epsilon. The master_* and clip_pad_* fields above describe only those three.
